question: to the Commission Willemien Koning (PPE), Sander Smit (ECR), Jeannette Baljeu (Renew) Subject:

Through sustainable fisheries partnership agreements (SFPAs), the EU facilitates access for EU fleets to tuna stocks in the waters of non-EU countries. Concurrently, the recovering eastern stock of Atlantic bluefin tuna is returning to the North Sea. Small-scale EU coastal fishers cannot benefit from this recovery, as national quota allocations rely on historical catch records rather than the current distribution of species. The absence of by-catch arrangements forces them to discard incidental catches, thus undermining the landing obligation. Meanwhile, the UK, having acquired a quota share, has opened a tuna fishery to small-scale vessels. Although quota allocation remains a national competence, Article 17 of the Common Fisheries Policy Regulation requires the Member States to apply socio-economic and environmental criteria when allocating fishing opportunities. 1.

How does the Commission assess the policy imbalance whereby the EU extensively supports international tuna fishing, yet provides no active framework to assist smallscale North Sea fishers in benefiting from locally returning stocks of Atlantic bluefin tuna?

In the light of its vade mecum on Article 171 and the upcoming simplification package, how will the Commission monitor and support Member States in applying this guidance to grant small-scale fishers access to emerging stocks via by-catch or trial quotas?

How does the Commission intend to address, at the upcoming annual meeting of the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas (ICCAT), the geographical scope of artisanal quota provisions in relation to northern EU waters?
